column3: Close to the Greek; “departure” (literally “exodus”) is rendered “decease.”
NKJV has “My beloved Son,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “My Son, the Chosen One.”
Close to the Greek; “unbelieving” is rendered “faithless.”
NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “all that He was doing.”
NKJV has “will be great,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “is great.”
NKJV has “against us … on our side,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “against you … for you.”
NKJV includes “just as Elijah did,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV adds “and said, ‘You do not know what manner of spirit you are of,’” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “He rebuked them.”
NKJV begins with “For the Son of Man did not come to destroy men's lives but to save them,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “And they went to another village.”
NKJV includes “Lord,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
Close to the Greek; “declare” is rendered “preach.”
